entities.summary: Flattening the curve is a public health strategy used to slow down the spread of an infectious disease in order to prevent overwhelming health care systems. The curve being flattened refers to the epidemic curve, a visual representation of the number of infected people needing health care over time. During an epidemic, health care systems can become overwhelmed when the number of people infected exceeds their capacity to provide adequate care. Flattening the curve reduces the peak number of infected people requiring care at any one time, helping ensure that the healthcare system remains within its capacity to treat patients.
